source.notes: Found on the official page https://cisce.org/specimen-question-papers-icse-class-x-2027/. This is a SPECIMEN paper for the 2027 ICSE examination (examYear=2027), not a past board exam. The single PDF contains both the question paper (13 printed pages, PDF pages 1–13) and a 'DRAFT MARKING SCHEME' (5 printed pages, PDF pages 14–18); answerSourceUrl is the same URL, answerSourceFile is null. Paper code printed on every page: 'T27 523 – SPECIMEN'. Section A (Question 1: 15 one-mark MCQ/assertion-reason items; Question 2: five 5-mark sub-questions (i)-(v)) is compulsory, 40 marks, per the printed instruction 'Section A is compulsory.' Section B prints 'Attempt any four questions from this Section' over six 10-mark questions (Questions 3-8); this is a pick-4-of-6 choice, NOT a standard two-alternative 'OR' pair, so choiceGroup is not used for these — all six are included as ordinary questions and a student attempting any four scores the printed maximum of 80. Because this pack (correctly) includes all six Section B questions, the sum of question marks in this file is 100 (40 Section A + 60 Section B), not 80; that is expected for a pick-4-of-6 paper, not an error. Some multi-part Section B sub-questions reference 'the above process' / 'this disorder' / 'this experiment' and cannot be answered standing alone, so they are kept together as one CASE_BASED/LONG_ANSWER entry per the brief; other sub-parts within the same numbered question are fully generic (no back-reference to the scenario) and are split into their own entries with their own chapter. Cognitive-level tags ('[Recall]', '[Understanding]', '[Application]', '[Analysis]') are printed next to most items; where a printed tag applies to exactly one question entry it is recorded as cognitiveLevel; where a merged multi-part entry covers several differently-tagged sub-parts, cognitiveLevel is omitted and the per-sub-part tags are listed in that entry's extractionIssues instead (the tag is kept out of the text field itself). In Question 1's marking scheme, options (a)-(d) and the 15 correct-letter/answer-text lists were printed in a two-column layout that pdftotext linearised into a scrambled block; all 15 correctOption values were verified by matching the answer text in that block against each option in the question paper (both agree consistently). In the marking scheme for Question 3, the printed sub-answer labels (iii) and (iv) are swapped relative to the question paper's own (iii)/(iv) order (the content that answers QP question (iv) is printed under marking-scheme label (iii), and vice versa); officialAnswer text below is matched to each question by content, not by the marking scheme's own (possibly mislabelled) numbering, and this is flagged in that entry's extractionIssues. accessedOn 2026-09-28. Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

Reason (R): Plants have a well-developed hormonal system to respond to sunlight, gravity, water, etc.

questions.text:
Avinash placed a potted plant on a windowsill on a hot summer morning. By afternoon, the leaves had wilted though the soil was well watered. He moved the plant indoors and the leaves regained their turgidity.
(i) Name the process responsible for the wilting of leaves. (1)
(ii) Define the above process. (2)
(iii) Explain how the process will differ on a rainy day. (2)
(iv) Which are the primary pores through which the above process takes place? Where are they located? (2)
(v) List three adaptations in plants to reduce this process. (3)
extractionIssues: Sub-part marks shown in brackets were printed beside each part.

In the marking scheme, the printed answer labels (iii) and (iv) are swapped relative to this question's own (iii)/(iv) order: the marking scheme's '(iii)' contains the answer to this question's (iv) ('Stomata. Leaves and young green stems.'), and its '(iv)' contains the answer to this question's (iii) ('Rate of transpiration will be less...'). The officialAnswer below is matched to each part by content, not by the marking scheme's own numbering.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Transpiration
(ii) It is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant.
(iii) Rate of transpiration will be less as the atmosphere will have more humidity. Diffusion of water vapour from the plant to outside will be slow.
(iv) Stomata. Leaves and young green stems.
(v) Narrow leaves, thick cuticle, fewer stomata

questions.text: Why is haemophilia uncommon in human females?

officialAnswer.text: Females have 2 X chromosomes. If one carries the recessive gene, the dominant gene supresses the disease. Whereas males have only one X chromosome and if it has the recessive gene, they show the disease.

questions.text:
A potted plant under a bell jar with a watch glass containing potassium hydroxide is placed under sunlight for three hours. After exposure to sunlight none of the leaves of the plant “X” turned blue black when tested with iodine, while the leaves of the control plant “Y” did.
(i) What is the aim of the experiment? (1)
(ii) Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis. Name the mineral element essential for the formation of chlorophyll. (2)
(iii) Explain the conclusion drawn from this experiment after the iodine test. (2)
extractionIssues: Cognitive-level tags printed per sub-part: (i) Understanding, (ii) Recall, (iii) Analysis — not captured in a single cognitiveLevel field because they differ per sub-part.
Subscripts flattened: CO2, H2O, C6H12O6, O2.

The equation's 'Chlorophyll / Sunlight' reaction-arrow condition text was rendered as garbled, duplicated bold Unicode characters in the source PDF; reproduced here as plain text, flagged for verification against PDF page 17.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) To prove that CO2 is necessary for photosynthesis.
(ii) 6CO2 + 12H2O --[Chlorophyll, Sunlight]--> C6H12O6 + 6H2O + 6O2. Magnesium
(iii) Plant X – CO2 was absorbed by KOH. Photosynthesis did not take place. Starch was absent. Plant Y- CO2 was available for photosynthesis. Starch was prepared. So the leaves turn blue black during iodine test.

questions.text: State one difference between identical twins and fraternal twins.

officialAnswer.text: Identical twins- a single fertilised egg divides into two, to form two separate individuals of the same gender, i.e. either 2 boys or 2 girls. Fraternal twins- two fertilised eggs form two individuals. They may either be 2 boys or 2 girls or 1 boy and 1 girl.
